data.source_title: Considerations for Reducing Risk: Surfaces in Healthcare Facilities
data.locator: Core Components 1, 4–6; Standardized setting-specific cleaning protocols; discharge/transfer cleaning; lines 107–121 in the opened CDC page
data.source_setting: Acute-care hospitals; CDC environmental cleaning and disinfection considerations.
data.source_n: Not applicable; practice guidance, no observed cleaning episodes.
value: follow room-type- and risk-specific discharge/transfer cleaning protocol
identify room/equipment as cleaned and ready for use
communicate minimum cleaning-time expectations to bed control and nursing
track and audit cleaning processes and feed back results
data.source_evidence_basis: CDC explicitly recommends standardized terminal cleaning protocols by room type, pathogen/PPE considerations, ready-for-use identification, minimum cleaning times established by observation, awareness by patient-flow teams, and time tracking/audits.
data.limitations: The page does not supply a universal number of minutes; it directs facilities to establish minimum cleaning times through observation. Bedside teams may also have cleaning duties, so role ownership is local.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent room turnover as a task with local protocol, start/end timestamps, and a ready-state signal to bed management; do not insert a generic service-time value.
